subject: fix certain parameters to zero (actually disable them)

messages.author: ebb54efc2613d912
messages.subject: fix certain parameters to zero (actually disable them)
parts:
Dear all,
I'd like to test how the result of a biogeographic analysis changes if one would assume purely cladogenetic processes, so I'd like to disable all the anagenetic parameters. I tried so by setting them to zero (or actually a very small range from 1e-15 to 2e-15), but this threw some error (I forgot to copy it, I believe it was something with optimx and a non feasible state) and aborted the analysis. Does anyone know if there is a straight foreward way to do what I want? As far as I understood with BioGeoBEARS_model_defaults
one can set only minimum values but not maximum values.

Cheers

messages.author: 665b3d97beb30882
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] fix certain parameters to zero (actually disable them)
parts:
Hi,

The BioGeoBEARS parameters table:

BioGeoBEARS_run_object$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table

...allows you to set both the initial (init), min, and max of each parameter, and "type" sets whether each parameter is fixed or freely estimated.

However, optim and optimx require at least one free parameter, so that they have something to optimize. If you just want to fix all parameters and calculate the likelihood under that, you can do:

bears_optim_run(BioGeoBEARS_run_object, skip_optim=TRUE)

An alternative hack which is basically equivalent is to leave parameters "free", but give them very narrow min/max.

I think if you set d=0 and e=0 you will basically force the ancestor to be everywhere -- that, or it will crash, e.g., under the DEC model, (AB,CD) cannot be traced back to (ABCD) without some d and e events. DIVALIKE can do such a transition.

If you start making more cladogenetic parameters free, this is fine, but I haven't explored it, and it may take some new code to do a simplex-type setup.

Cheers!
Nick
